facts.label: IWF bodyweight-category changes and world-record reset (2025 and 2026)
facts.display: Aug 2026 World Standards = 98% of a trendline fitted to prior records (June 2025 percentage unverified)
facts.who_when: IWF; categories effective 1 Jun 2025, revised again effective 1 Aug 2026
facts.notes: From 1 Jun 2025 the IWF cut to eight categories per sex. Men: 60, 65, 71, 79, 88, 94, 110, +110 kg (BarBend's June 2025 article listed 98 kg instead of 94). Earlier records were frozen as historical, and 'World Standards' became the minimum lift that counts as a world record. From 1 Aug 2026 (aligned to LA28) the men's categories are 60, 65, 70, 75, 85, 95, 110, +110 kg. ASOIF says the new reference values came from a trendline 'adjusted to 98%', and that men's 60, 65, 110 and +110 kept their records. So the heaviest current marks (+110 kg) are post-2025 records, and Talakhadze's heavier lifts are historical. Editor change: both verifiers flagged the researcher's June 2025 '97%' figure and the 'beat by at least 1 kg' rule as unconfirmed. IWF pages return 403, and neither BarBend nor Wikipedia states them, so the headline value is now the confirmed 0.98 (2026). ASOIF says only that 2025 used 'the same mathematical model'.

Misiorowski's 105.5 mph (27 Jun 2026) is the fastest pitch by a starter and 'the third-fastest pitch recorded in the Statcast Era', so the record stands. The glossary says Statcast velocity is the maximum speed 'with the max speed always being at the release point'; that describes Statcast (from 2015), and the 2010 pitch was tracked by PITCHf/x, so 'at release' is our inference, as is the idea that the earlier 105.1 mph (SABR) was the same pitch measured farther from the hand. MLB does not say how the 105.8 was derived. Skeptic: misquote of Misiorowski fixed; 'at release' removed from label and display; inferences labelled.

facts.who_when: Keith Liddell (USA), 2013 (beat his own 44 mph from 2012), Body Tac Karate Dojo, Chicago

facts.label: Boxer punch fist speed (lab-measured)
facts.display: Peak about 6.6-12.5 m/s; best group-mean peak 11.95 m/s (amateur lead hook)
facts.who_when: Whiting, Gregor & Finerman 1988; Piorkowski, Lees & Barton 2011; Stanley et al. 2018; Liu et al. 2022
facts.notes: Whiting et al. 1988 (Am J Sports Med 16(2):130-136): only four experienced boxers, filmed with two synchronized cameras. Peak fist speed 6.6-12.5 m/s, reached 8-21 ms before contact; contact speed 5.9-8.2 m/s. Piorkowski et al. 2011 (10 competition-standard boxers, 8-camera system): mean contact speed of single maximal punches across four punch types 9.26 +/- 2.09 m/s, with hooks faster. They cite Atha et al. 1985 at 8.9 m/s for 'one professional boxer', unnamed in the source (the researcher's 'Frank Bruno' is removed), and Walilko 2005 at 8.16 m/s for amateurs. Stanley et al. 2018 (15 male amateurs): lead hook peak 11.95 +/- 1.84 m/s, the fastest punch type. Label corrected from 'elite': 11.95 is an amateur mean. Straight punches are slower: elite lead straight peak 7.16 +/- 0.48 m/s (Liu 2022). Karate punches at 10-15 m/s come from a 1979 Scientific American article, seen only through Science.ca, which does not name the authors. Peak speed and contact speed are different quantities.

facts.label: Hill force-velocity equation (form) and eccentric limits
facts.display: (F + a)(v + b) = (F0 + a) b; v = b(F0 - F)/(F + a); vmax = b F0 / a. Eccentric: about 1.6-1.8 F0 in isolated animal muscle (up to about 2.0 F0 in some fits); about 1.3-1.4 F0 human in vivo
facts.who_when: A.V. Hill 1938 (frog sartorius); reviewed by Alcazar et al. 2019, Front Physiol 10:769
facts.notes: F is force, v is shortening velocity, F0 is maximal isometric force; a has force units and b has velocity units. Hill's own fit: (F + 14.4)(V + 1.0) = (70.6 + 14.4) x 1.0. The ratio a/F0 sets the curvature; a smaller ratio means a more curved relation. The equation is empirical and covers concentric (shortening) contractions only. Editor settlement on eccentric force, after fetching the full Alcazar 2019 text: the verifiers quoted different sentences, and both are in the review. It says an eccentric hyperbolic function 'levels off at ~1.6-2.0 P0 in muscle preparations (Mashima et al., 1972)'. It compares human with animal maximal eccentric force as '~1.3 vs. ~1.6-1.8 P0'. It says properly assessed human eccentric force should exceed isometric force by 'up to 1.4 P0' (Hahn 2018). For a human-calibrated model, cap eccentric force at about 1.3-1.4 F0.

sources.title: Alcazar et al. 2019, On the shape of the force-velocity relationship in skeletal muscles, Front Physiol 10:769

facts.label: Hill curvature parameter a/F0
facts.display: Typical 0.25 (convention); 0.18-0.32 for single muscles or joints; multi-joint leg press mean 1.06 +/- 0.72 (near-linear)
facts.who_when: Hill 1938; Edman et al. 1976; Martin, Martin & Morlon 1994; Riviere et al. 2023
facts.notes: 0.25 is a widely used normalization convention, not a measured human population mean. Single-muscle values: Hill 1938 frog sartorius about 0.20 (computed from his fit, 14.4/70.6); Edman et al. 1976 fibres averaged 0.28 before truncating data at 78% P0 and 0.18 after (Alcazar 2019). The researcher's '0.18-0.29' is corrected to 0.18-0.28. Human in vivo (Martin et al. 1994, Eur J Appl Physiol 69:539-544, abstract): best-fit curvature parameter 'af' of 0.28 for the ankle extensors and 0.32 for the elbow flexors. The abstract says af 'affects the curvature', but that af equals a/F0 is not confirmed from full text. Whole-limb, multi-joint horizontal leg press (Riviere et al. 2023, 9 trained adults, 8 men and 1 woman): mean a/F0 1.06 +/- 0.72, and the authors prefer a linear model. Both verifiers noted that the researcher's 0.53-2.70 were three example participants, not the study range. a/F0 falls as temperature rises (Alcazar). The researcher's claim that slow-twitch muscle is more curved is removed, because Alcazar lists 'type of muscle' as a factor without a direction. Use about 0.25 for single muscles and expect a much flatter curve at whole-limb level.

sources.title: Alcazar et al. 2019, Front Physiol 10:769
Martin, Martin & Morlon 1994, Eur J Appl Physiol 69(6):539-544 (record)
Riviere et al. 2023, Sports Medicine - Open (low force-high velocity domain in lower-limb extensions)

facts.label: Vertical takeoff velocity of the centre of mass, elite jumpers
facts.who_when: Derived: v = sqrt(2 g h) with h = 1.1684 m (Sensabaugh 46 in) gives 4.79 m/s; Helene & Yamashita 2005 high-jump model gives 4.5 m/s
facts.notes: A physics estimate (g = 9.80665 m/s^2), not a measurement. No peer-reviewed force-plate value for elite jumpers was found. Jump-and-reach overstates centre-of-mass rise, so 4.79 m/s is an upper bound for standing jumps. The unverified 47.1 in jump would give 4.84 m/s. The 4.5 m/s is a model output for a running high jump with a 7.5 m/s approach; one verifier confirmed it from the full text. Dapena's ISBS abstract gives no numbers.

facts.label: Peak vertical ground reaction force in elite maximal-speed sprinting
facts.display: About 4.1-5.0 x body weight per step (stance average up to about 2.5 x)
facts.who_when: Clark & Weyand 2014 (J Appl Physiol 117:604-615) via secondary sources; Coh et al. 2018; Coh 2019
facts.notes: Weyand's group, via Scientific American 2016 and NASE, citing Clark & Weyand 2014: elite peaks up to about 5.0 x body weight, against about 3.5 x for capable non-sprinters. Editor settlement of the verifier disagreement, after fetching NASE: the page says elite stance-averaged forces are 'as large as 2.5 times body mass', so that figure stands (2.0 x for less swift runners). Kinematic estimates for Bolt at about 12.1 m/s (Zagreb 2011, two high-speed cameras): 4.2 x body weight = 3,932 N, contact 86 ms (Coh 2018). Coh 2019 gives 3,956.74 N and calls it 4.1 x, but with 95 kg and g = 9.80665 that is 4.25 x, so the paper is inconsistent. The primary Clark & Weyand text was not read.

facts.label: Barefoot plantar contact area of one adult foot, quiet standing
facts.display: About 71-95 cm^2 per foot (static); about 112-140 cm^2 per foot in walking stance
facts.who_when: Kang et al. 2024 (J Korean Foot Ankle Soc 28(1):21-26); Kuruma et al. 2023 (World Physiotherapy Congress abstract)
facts.notes: Kang 2024, static barefoot standing, normal-foot group of 15 (whole cohort healthy male volunteers, mean age 23.5): EMED-n50 79.66 +/- 11.82 cm^2 and HR Mat 70.72 +/- 13.80 cm^2. Dynamic values: 139.96 and 111.85 cm^2. Only one foot per subject was analysed, so these are per-foot values (an inference from the methods; the table does not say 'per foot'). Kuruma 2023 (30 adults, 18 men, SR Soft Vision): 190.5 +/- 30.6 cm^2 for both feet, about 95 cm^2 per foot. Contact area depends on the device and sensor threshold. Shifting weight onto one foot, or onto the forefoot at push-off, changes it.

sources.title: Kang et al. 2024, Comparative Analysis of Two Pedobarography Systems, J Korean Foot Ankle Soc
Kuruma et al. 2023, Effect of foot band on foot alignment in standing posture (World Physiotherapy Congress)

facts.label: Palm area of one adult hand (length x width estimate)
facts.display: Palm about 74-78 cm^2; whole hand about 132-147 cm^2 (length x width rectangles, which overestimate true contact)
facts.who_when: Agarwal & Sahu 2010, Indian J Plast Surg 43(1):49-53 (300 adults)
facts.notes: Adult means: male palm 77.853 +/- 10.29 cm^2, female palm 73.659 +/- 9.14 cm^2. Whole hand including fingers: male 146.5 cm^2, female 132.4 cm^2. Method corrected (both verifiers agree): these are not traced outline areas. The paper multiplies hand width by hand length or palm length, so the values are rectangles that overestimate the true outline, especially for the whole hand with its tapering fingers. Real flat-surface contact is smaller still because the palm is hollow. Treat all values as upper bounds. The population is small-bodied (mean body surface area 1.59 m^2 male, 1.44 m^2 female). As ratios, the palm is about 0.50% and the hand about 0.92% of body surface area, so scale up for larger bodies. The high bound is the whole hand, not the palm alone.

sources.title: Agarwal & Sahu 2010, Determination of hand and palm area as a ratio of body surface area in Indian population

gaps: Process limit: the shared web-search budget ran out before this final edit, so editor checks were done only by fetching known pages directly. That covered the Alcazar 2019 full text, the NASE summary of Clark & Weyand, Wikipedia's Hammer throw, Weightlifting records and Byron Jones pages, the Guinness weight-sustained page, and Kang 2024. No fresh searches could be run for records newer than the sources: silver dollar or Hummer tire deadlift after 2022, Atlas stone after 2023, a heavier multi-ply deadlift or squat, Combine verticals 2021-2026, or throws late in the 2026 season.

IWF June 2025 World Standards: the researcher's 97% figure and the 'beat the standard by at least 1 kg' rule are unconfirmed. IWF pages return 403, and BarBend and Wikipedia do not state them. Only the Aug 2026 98% trendline rule (ASOIF) is confirmed. The +110 kg snatch World Standard (said to be 218 kg) was not seen in any source.

OpenPowerlifting's all-time multi-ply rankings did not load. So it is not confirmed that Andy Bolton's 457.5 kg (2009) is still the heaviest equipped deadlift, or Nathan Baptist's about 595 kg the heaviest equipped squat.
Drug-testing status of the WRPF meet where Engelbrecht pulled 492.5 kg is unknown.

Pull records (aircraft, vehicle, house, bus, train, teeth): no source gives a measured pulling force or rolling-resistance coefficient, so the sim must model rolling resistance itself. No Guinness page was found for the 2025 Cairo train pull, and AP's '279 tons' does not say which ton.

Bus pull (upper body): the MTA release (33,440 lb) returns 403 and no Guinness page was found. Only UPI's 33,400 lb is readable. The exact date (20 Sep 2021), the seated method and the adjudicator are unverified.

Back lifts (Ernst, Anderson, Cyr), the hip lift, the carousel lift and the Hummer tire deadlift have no documented lift height or bar start height, so work and energy cannot be computed. Whether Rauno Heinla wore a suit for the 580 kg silver dollar deadlift is disputed between sources.
Louis Cyr's back lift: year, city and weight differ between sources (1895 Boston 1,967 kg vs 1896 Chicago 4,133 lb).
Nick Best's 1,266 kg carousel lift was a TV production with no stated sanctioning; the filming date was not found. No hip-lift record after 2012 was checked.
Weight sustained on body: Guinness gives no hold time or body position and does not name the previous holder (the title was 'previously broken back in 2023').
The 2026 World Log Lift Challenge (Glasgow, 17 Oct 2026) is after today and could change the 231 kg log record.
Usain Bolt: only a 20 m split average (12.42 m/s) is available. No instantaneous, laser-measured peak from the 2009 Berlin biomechanics report (Graubner & Nixdorf 2011) was retrieved.
Clark & Weyand 2014 (peak and stance-averaged ground reaction force) and Fleisig 1999 (ball speed by playing level) were seen only through secondary sources.
No measured (force-plate or motion-capture) takeoff vertical velocity for elite jumpers was found; that entry is a derived estimate.
No authoritative human population mean for Hill a/F0 exists in the sources; 0.25 is a convention. Whether Martin et al. 1994's 'af' equals a/F0 was not confirmed from full text.

The method behind the Guinness 'fastest martial arts punch' (45 mph) is undocumented. The karate fist speeds of 10-15 m/s (1979 Scientific American) and Atha 1985 (8.9 m/s) were seen only through secondary citations.

Unverified side claims dropped from notes: Yousefi 262 kg at the 2024 Worlds, Jesus Olivares 485 kg squat (Oct 2026), Vispy Kharadi 1,819 kg (Feb 2025), Alekna pectoral surgery, Eli Stowers 'TE record', Misiorowski 'starter record', and the Chapman 105.7 mph (2016) and Joyce 105.5 mph (2024) figures.
The 47.1 in vertical (Josh Imatorbhebhe, 2015, jump mat) and Willie Creear's 47 in regional-combine jump are unverified and left out of the facts.

Static plantar contact area depends on the device and sensor threshold, so no single normative adult value exists. The Kang 2024 cohort was all male. Palm and hand areas are length-by-width rectangles from a small-bodied population and overestimate real contact area.
